Agent Name: Planner
Step Number: 1
Reason for Mistake: The Planner made a fundamental error in comparing the masses of subatomic particles. It incorrectly stated that the electron mass ($9.11 \times 10^{-31}$ kg) is greater than the proton mass ($1.67 \times 10^{-27}$ kg) by comparing the exponents (31 > 27) without accounting for the base values. In scientific notation, a smaller negative exponent (or larger positive exponent in the denominator context, though here it is $10^{-31}$ vs $10^{-27}$) indicates a much smaller number. Specifically, $10^{-27}$ is 1,000,000 times larger than $10^{-31}$. Consequently, the electron is significantly lighter than the proton. Because the electron has the smallest mass among the options, losing an electron results in the least mass loss, making the correct answer D. The Planner's logic led to the wrong conclusion (A) based on this mathematical misunderstanding.
